title: Demurrage and Detention Free Time: Disputed Amount as the Limit on a Dispute Credit
content:
## Principle

Under Demurrage and Detention Free Time, a dispute credit against a record's demurrage charges is the desk's ruling on a dispute that the billed party itself has on file against that line and that is awaiting decision, standing as submitted. What such a ruling can give back is capped by the amount that the dispute puts in issue: the disputed amount recorded on the most recently lodged dispute against the line that still shows submitted. The credit entry names that dispute as well as the line.

Where no dispute against the line shows submitted, nothing is in issue: there is no disputed amount to cap a credit, and the credit available on the line is nothing.

## Input, judgement, output

| Disputes found against the demurrage line | Figure that caps the credit |
|---|---|
| one, submitted, disputed amount 800.00 (hypothetical) | 800.00 |
| two, an earlier one withdrawn and a later one submitted at 500.00 (hypothetical) | 500.00, the figure on the submitted dispute |
| one, withdrawn | none: no dispute is awaiting decision, so no credit arises |
| none | none: no credit arises |

## Points of judgement

- The disputed amount is taken exactly as it stands on the dispute record; the desk does not substitute a figure of its own.
- The line in question is the record's demurrage invoice line, identified by its invoice reference.
